---
title: App gallery
description: Browse, search, pin and open every Rayfin app you can open in Fabric, see which need attention, take a quick look at one, and start a new app from an example.
---

The app gallery shows every Rayfin app you can open in Microsoft Fabric: the apps you publish
from this computer, the apps you published from another computer, and the apps other people share
with you. Search them, see where each one lives, when it was last published and which need
attention, take a quick look at one, and open them in your browser, in Fabric, or in Fabricator.

![The app gallery with eleven sample apps as cards, each with its workspace and when it was last published, and the details of Contoso Expenses open beside them with Open app, Open in Fabric, Open in Fabricator and Copy link](/screenshots/app-gallery.webp)

## Open the app gallery

- On **Your projects**, select **App gallery**.
- Or press `Ctrl+K` (`⌘K` on macOS), type `gallery`, and select **App gallery**. You can open it this
  way while you work on an app, too.

To leave, select **Back to projects** in the app bar, or **Back to** your project's name when you
opened the gallery from a project. You can also press `Esc`.

## Sign in to Azure

The gallery finds your apps with your Azure CLI sign-in. Signing in to Azure is optional at setup,
so if you skipped it, the gallery shows **Sign in to Azure** and "Fabricator finds the apps you can
open with your Azure sign-in. Sign in to Azure to see them."

1. Select **Sign in to Azure**.
2. Finish signing in in your browser. The gallery then lists your apps.

The gallery lists the apps the Azure CLI's account can open. Under the gallery's title, "Every
Rayfin app you can open in Fabric, as" names that account. It can be a different account from the
Fabric account you publish with. To use another account, see
[Use more than one Azure CLI account](/docs/start/accounts#use-more-than-one-azure-cli-account).

## Find an app

Each app is a card with a picture of the app, its name, its workspace, and its description when it
has one. Below them, small dots and words say more:

- What may need looking at: **Publish failed**, **Changes not published** when its project on this
  computer changed since it was published, or `Rayfin <version> available` when a newer Rayfin is
  out for it. See
  [Find the apps that need attention](/docs/build/app-gallery#find-the-apps-that-need-attention).
- **On this computer**: a project in Fabricator publishes this app.
- A team workspace's name: the app is that team workspace's published app. A teammate's preview
  says **Team preview**. These show when **Team workspaces** is turned on in
  **Settings → Experiments**.
- When the app was last published, such as "Published 3 days ago", or "Not published yet".

To find an app:

- Type in the search box. It matches app names and descriptions, workspace and team workspace
  names, and the names of your projects. Press `/` to get to the search box from anywhere in the
  gallery.
- Select **All**, **On this computer** or **In Fabric only** to see every app, only the apps a
  project on this computer publishes, or only the others. Each shows how many apps it has.
- Select **Needs attention** to see only the apps that need looking at, or **Apps I can edit** to
  see only the apps in workspaces where you're an Admin, Member or Contributor. Select it again to
  see every app.
- Pick a workspace in **All workspaces** to see only its apps. Its menu lists under **Recent**
  the workspaces your apps on this computer use, most recently used first, with when you last
  used each, and under **Other workspaces** the rest, each with how many apps it has. A
  workspace a tool named, such as `replit-data-dashboard-2e377200-…`, shows as a title, such as
  Replit data dashboard, with its name below. Type in **Search workspaces** to find one, and
  press Enter to pick the first match.
- Sort by **Name**, **Recently published**, **Recently opened** or **Workspace**. **Recently
  opened** puts first the apps you opened last from the gallery or from Search, and the apps whose
  projects you opened last in Fabricator. **Workspace** groups the apps under their workspaces'
  names, with the workspaces your apps on this computer use first.

Select **Table** beside the number of apps to see the apps as a table, one row each with its
workspace, when it was published, what needs looking at and where it is: handy when you can open
many apps. Select **Cards** to go back.

Fabricator remembers your choices of filters, order and layout for the next time you open the
gallery.

## Pictures of your apps

A card shows a picture of the app when Fabricator has one. Fabricator draws it from the preview of
an app on this computer, as it does for **Your projects**, and the gallery shows it on the app that
project publishes.

When you publish an app from Fabricator, its picture goes out with the app's files as
`fabricator-thumbnail.webp`, so other people's galleries can show it too. Fabricator puts the file
in the app's `public` folder only while it publishes, and takes it out again before it saves a
version, so your project's files don't change. Other people's galleries show the picture when the
app's hosted files are public. See
[Static content hosting](https://rayfin.ai/docs/hosting) in the Rayfin docs.

Until there's a picture, a card shows the app's first letters on its own color.

## Find the apps that need attention

**Needs attention** shows the apps where something may need looking at, with how many there are:

| What it says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| **Publish failed** | The app's last publish from this computer didn't finish, or Fabric says its latest publish failed. |
| **Changes not published** | Its project on this computer changed since it was last published. |
| `Rayfin <version> available` | A newer Rayfin is out for its project on this computer. Open the project to update it. See [Keep Rayfin up to date](/docs/ship/rayfin-versions). |
| **Not published yet** | The app exists in Fabric, but hasn't published its pages. |

The gallery checks what Fabric says about each app's publishes as it shows it, so with **Needs
attention** on, the count can grow for a moment while it checks every app.

## Open an app

Select an app's card to see its details beside the gallery: when it was last published, its
address, its workspace, whether you can change it (**Your access**), and its project and team
workspace when it has them.

- **Open app** opens the app in your browser.
- **Quick look** shows the live app over the gallery. See
  [Take a quick look at an app](/docs/build/app-gallery#take-a-quick-look-at-an-app).
- **Open in Fabric** opens the app's page in the Fabric portal.
- **Open in Fabricator** opens the project that publishes the app. Only apps marked **On this
  computer** have it.
- **Copy link** copies the app's address, or the link to its page in Fabric when Fabricator doesn't
  know its address.
- **Pin to the top** keeps the app first in the gallery. See
  [Pin the apps you use most](/docs/build/app-gallery#pin-the-apps-you-use-most).

An app that hasn't published its pages yet says "This app hasn’t published its pages yet." When
Fabric doesn't say where an app is, its details say "Fabric didn’t share this app’s address. Open it
in Fabric instead."

To close the details, select the close button or press `Esc`.

Fabric apps also show up in Search: press `Ctrl+K` (`⌘K` on macOS) and type an app's name to open
it. See [Search](/docs/start/search).

## Take a quick look at an app

A quick look shows an app's live page over the gallery, so you can try it without leaving
Fabricator.

1. Select an app's card, so it has the focus.
2. Press `Space`. Or select **Quick look** in the app's details.

The app's name and address are along the top, with **Open app** and **Open in Fabric**. Sign in to
the app there as you would in your browser. To put it away, press `Space` or `Esc`, or select the
close button.

An app has a quick look once Fabricator knows its address.

## Give an app a description

Most apps have no description in Fabric, because Rayfin's publish doesn't set one. A description
helps everyone who can open the app find it in the gallery and in Fabric.

When you publish an app from Fabricator and it has no description, Copilot writes a one-sentence
description from the app's files and what you asked for in its chat, and Fabricator saves it in
Fabric. It never replaces a description the app already has.

To write one for an app now:

1. Select the app's card. It has to be an app a project on this computer publishes, in a
   workspace where you're an Admin, Member or Contributor.
2. Under "No description yet", select **Write a description**.

## Start from an example

Select **Examples** at the top of the gallery to see community apps to start from. Select **Use
this example** on one to open **New project** with that example chosen. See
[Start from a community example](/docs/build/projects#start-from-a-community-example).

## Pin the apps you use most

Pin an app to keep it at the top of the gallery.

1. Hover over the app's card.
2. In the card's top-right corner, select **Pin to the top**.

You can also select **Pin to the top** in the app's details.

A pinned app keeps its pin in sight and comes first, whichever order you pick:

- **Name**, **Recently published** and **Recently opened** show the pinned apps first, in the same
  order, then the others.
- **Workspace** groups the pinned apps under **Pinned**, above the workspaces.

Search and the filters still apply, so a pinned app that doesn't match them isn't shown.

To unpin an app, select its pin again, or select **Unpin** in its details.

Fabricator remembers your pinned apps for the next time you open the gallery.

## Keep the gallery up to date

When you open the gallery again, it shows the apps it found last time while it checks Fabric again,
and says "Checking Fabric…" until it's done. To check now, select the **Refresh** button next to
**Cards** and **Table**.

If checking again doesn't work, the gallery keeps showing the apps it found before, with what went
wrong above them. When your Azure sign-in has expired, it says "Sign in to Azure to see your latest
apps. These are from earlier." Select **Sign in to Azure**.

## An app is missing from the gallery

The gallery shows only the Rayfin apps the Azure CLI's account can open.

1. Under the gallery's title, check which account it reads with. If it's the wrong one, switch the
   Azure CLI to the right account in **Accounts**. See
   [Azure CLI is signed in to the wrong account](/docs/troubleshooting/setup-and-sign-in#azure-cli-is-signed-in-to-the-wrong-account).
2. Make sure the account can open the app in Fabric: someone has to share the app with you, or add
   you to its workspace. See [Share your app](/docs/ship/share).
3. Select **Refresh**.

If you can open more apps than Fabricator reads at once, the gallery says "Fabric has more apps than
Fabricator reads at once, so some apps you can open aren’t shown."

If the gallery says "Couldn’t list your apps", select **Try again**. If it still fails,
[Report a problem](/docs/troubleshooting/report-a-problem).
